runs.question: When did Apollo 8 launch, and who was its crew?
runs.expected: 1968-12-21, with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders.
runs.answer: Apollo 8 launched on 1968-12-21 (apollo-8: "Launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders"). Its crew was Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders (apollo-8). Jim Lovell is listed as flying Apollo 8 in December 1968, the first crewed lunar orbit (jim-lovell). The launch vehicle was the Saturn V, which flew its first crew on Apollo 8 (saturn-v). Apollo 8 was part of the Apollo program (apollo-program). Note: the edges list only Jim Lovell as Apollo 8's crew member; Frank Borman and Bill Anders are named in the apollo-8 fact line, so that part comes from the fact lines rather than the edges.

runs.answer: Beech Aircraft built the Apollo service module oxygen tanks, working under prime contractor North American Aviation [beech-aircraft] [north-american-aviation]. The tank in question was Oxygen tank No. 2 [oxygen-tank-2], which Beech Aircraft built [oxygen-tank-2]. North American Aviation was the prime contractor for the command and service module [north-american-aviation]. Note: the edges say North American Aviation subcontracted Beech Aircraft, which is consistent with this.

runs.question: When did NASA announce lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode?
runs.expected: 1962-07-11, chosen over direct ascent and Earth orbit rendezvous.
runs.answer: NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (lunar-orbit-rendezvous, src: NASA history). The lines also say the Apollo program adopted it as its mission mode in 1962 (apollo-program), which is consistent with that date. It was chosen over direct ascent and Earth orbit rendezvous (lunar-orbit-rendezvous), and it required a separate lander that became the lunar module (lunar-orbit-rendezvous, lunar-module). The lines do not give the exact day for the apollo-program claim, so only the 1962-07-11 date comes from the lunar-orbit-rendezvous fact line.

This is consistent with six crewed lunar landings between July 1969 and December 1972 (apollo-program: "Made six crewed lunar landings between July 1969 and December 1972"), and Apollo 17 in December 1972 was the last crewed lunar mission (apollo-program). Apollo 11's Eagle landing on 1969-07-20 (apollo-11) is one such landing. [derived] Two astronauts per landing across six landings gives twelve, matching the stated count.

Note: the square/round mismatch is the stated reason; the fact lines do not elaborate further on why the adapter was needed beyond this shape incompatibility. runs.answer: A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee (apollo-1). It happened at Launch Complex 34 at Cape Kennedy (apollo-1). It led to a command module redesign that included a quick-opening hatch (apollo-1). The command and service module was redesigned and built by North American Aviation (command-service-module, north-american-aviation). [derived] North American Aviation's oxygen tank heater specification was revised in 1965 to run at 65 volts, and its reviews missed that the tank's thermostatic switches were never changed (north-american-aviation); this is an inference that it relates to the cabin fire, which the lines do not state directly.

His exposure of the crews led to the rubella crew swap (rubella-crew-swap). Apollo 13 was commanded by Jim Lovell (apollo-13, jim-lovell; Apollo 13 Mission page). Therefore the mission Charlie Duke was a backup for, Apollo 13, was commanded by Jim Lovell. runs.question: Which company's revised specification set the voltage that the Apollo 13 tank switches could not handle?
runs.expected: North American Aviation, which revised the heater specification to 65 volts in 1965; the switches were built for 28 volts.
runs.answer: North American Aviation revised the oxygen tank heater specification in 1965 to run at 65 volts, but the tank's thermostatic switches were never changed, so they could not handle the higher voltage (north-american-aviation; oxygen-tank-2). Beech Aircraft, which built the tanks, did not change the switches when the specification moved to 65 volts (beech-aircraft). The switches were originally built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (oxygen-tank-2). The Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (apollo-13-review-board). [derived] The answer to 'whose revised specification' is North American Aviation, since it was the party that revised the heater specification to 65 volts; the switch failure itself is attributed to the mismatch between that revision and the unchanged switches.
